subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic Feishu group-sender subagents as an opt-in Feishu plugin capability, and what security/lifecycle contract must it use?
rationale: The implementation shape affects shared-chat authorization, memory isolation, tool permissions, durable config writes, and resource lifecycle, which cannot be safely chosen from source inspection alone.

options.title: Sponsor an opt-in Feishu design
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical design item and require a maintainer-approved Feishu plugin contract for auth, memory, skills, lifecycle, quotas, and admin commands before code lands.

options.title: Limit scope to session routing
options.body: Treat current group_sender/group_topic_sender session scoping as the supported path and close or narrow any persistent-agent work unless concrete gaps remain.

options.title: Move to external plugin experimentation
options.body: Ask interested teams to prototype the orchestration as an external plugin or ClawHub package first, then bring back missing SDK hooks if needed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor an opt-in Feishu design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical design item and require a maintainer-approved Feishu plugin contract for auth, memory, skills, lifecycle, quotas, and admin commands before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin is documented as community maintained by @m1heng, making them the best available owner for Feishu-specific product and security direction.
